KV bounds (8KiB value, 256 entries, 64KiB total, 128 key, derived file cap, depth 16) equal plugin_runtime/store.rs. No altered bound; PR body justifies the KV deviation. MIN_SESSION_GRID_DIM=1 has no named Core counterpart (Core literal 1..=) — semantics identical, not a defect.

Deltas are extraction-necessitated only (ViewId->u64, no Overlay variant, LuaValue->JsonValue, BridgeError->StoreError, std::fs directly). Transcript/history are types-only (descriptors + pure select_for_deletion + validate_record, no persistence) per plan non-goals; TRANSCRIPT_/HISTORY_ bounds are greenfield with no Core counterpart, as documented.

All 4 CodeRabbit fixes verified applied correctly + 1 decline verified correct:

1. UNIQUE TEMPS + AGE-GATED SWEEP: save_bytes_atomic now commits via unique_temp_sibling_for (pid + thread-id + atomic seq); sweep is age-gated (STALE_TEMP_AGE_SECS=3600, unknown-mtime treated as live/kept) with tightened prefix match (.tmp. / .tmp-). Live concurrent temps are seconds old and never swept; concurrent savers use distinct temps, each rename atomic (last-writer-wins, no torn state). No atomicity regression. New tests: sweep_never_deletes_live_temps, concurrent_saves_to_same_path_all_succeed.

2. CAPPED STREAMING LOAD: load_bytes_capped streams via File::take(cap+1) on a single open handle (no metadata pre-check TOCTOU), drains-and-counts the tail for exact TooLarge reports, max cap+1 bytes buffered. Grep confirms no bare std::fs::read remains on untrusted paths (only read_dir, dir-fsync open, streaming open). KvStore::load now routes through load_bytes_capped (NotFound stays clean start, rest via map_load_error) — closes the unbounded-alloc gap noted in PX-0010.

3. PURGE RESULT SEMANTICS: NotFound -> Ok(file_removed:false), other removal errors -> Err E_STORE_IO with memory left intact; file removed BEFORE entries cleared. Ordering is crash-safe: a crash between file-remove and memory-clear loses the process memory too, and the next load sees no file -> clean start. Doc accurately states failed purge leaves file + state intact. New test: purge_distinguishes_missing_file_from_removal_failure.

4. DECLINE (session_codec 714-722) CORRECT: independently confirmed Core session.rs:876-881 counts only explicit Some(Primary), and Core resolve_attachment/encode_session resolve None via derive_startup_owner identically to the port (port 728-742, 754-805 vs Core 888-937, 929-1000). Counting resolved attachments would DIVERGE the port from Core, which the W-146 plan forbids. Decline reply on the inline thread states this rationale. The Core-side attachment-counting edge (startup-owner None + explicit Primary elsewhere) is a TRACKED FOLLOW-UP for CTX-0939 — Core owns validation — not a demand on this PR.

5. PANEL-SCOPED RETENTION: select_for_deletion returns (panel,id) pairs; sort key and membership filter are (panel,id)-scoped; TranscriptDeletionEvidence.removed is Vec<(u64,u64)>. No remaining bare-segment-id filtering in src (only evidence.removed.len() count in tests). New tests: shared_segment_ids_stay_panel_scoped, byte_caps_count_each_panels_copy.

(1) NO UNBOUNDED I/O: drain-the-tail loop and LOAD_DRAIN_BUF_BYTES removed; grep confirms no drain/into_inner/bare-fs::read remains in src. Over-cap path reads at most cap+1 bytes (Take guard) then returns immediately — a multi-GB sparse file triggers only ~cap+1 bytes of I/O.
(2) FAIL-CLOSED PRESERVED: oversize returns Err(TooLarge), never Ok(partial); Ok only when bytes.len() <= cap; boundary cap==len still succeeds (new test within_cap_load_returns_exact_bytes).
(3) WITHIN-CAP EXACT UNCHANGED: take(cap+1)+read_to_end path untouched for the success case; byte-identical content asserted.
(4) SATURATION CONTRACT DOCUMENTED on both load_bytes_capped and the LoadError::TooLarge variant ('actual saturates at limit+1, means over cap, never exact'). All consumers (lib.rs FileBackend, kv.rs map_load_error, session_codec conversion) only forward actual into display strings — no exact-size logic. All test assertions expect saturation (incl. cap=len-1 case yielding actual==len==cap+1). No caller/test assumes exact over-cap sizes.
